classification.difficultyReason: Recognise simultaneous ringing as a least-common-multiple problem, rescale fractional periods into common whole-number units and convert the earliest recurrence back to seconds.

content.prompt: Four bells start tolling together and ring every $1$, $1\frac{1}{4}$, $1\frac{1}{5}$ and $1\frac{1}{6}$ seconds, respectively. After what period of time will they first ring all together again?

answer.short:
210 seconds.

Express the intervals in a common time unit and find their least common multiple.
answer.worked:
In units of $\frac{1}{60}$ second, the four intervals are:
$$\begin{align*}1&=\frac{60}{60}\\1\frac{1}{4}&=\frac{75}{60}\\1\frac{1}{5}&=\frac{72}{60}\\1\frac{1}{6}&=\frac{70}{60}\end{align*}$$
Find the least common multiple by listing multiples.
The first common multiple of $60$ and $75$ is $300$. Their common multiples are $300,600,900,1200,1500,1800,\ldots$; the first divisible by $72$ is $1800$.
Common multiples of $60$, $75$ and $72$ are therefore $1800,3600,5400,7200,9000,10800,12600,\ldots$. The first divisible by $70$ is $12600$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Time}&=12600\div60\\&=210\text{ seconds}\end{align*}$$
